name: GPU-based Voxelization via Slice Rendering
definition: A technique that computes the voxelization of a mesh by using hardware rasterization. It renders the mesh from different points of view, adjusting Znear/Zfar planes for each slice, and compiles the results into a final 3D grid. All computation is handled on the GPU.
summary: GPU-based Voxelization via Slice Rendering converts triangle meshes into 3D voxel grids by using hardware rasterization to project geometry slice-by-slice, offering a fast, GPU-only alternative to CPU-based methods.
